attribution.note: Marcus adopts the allegation in his own prose, citing Fortune as its basis.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the asserted non-delivery and records the Fortune qualifier. This is a retrospective observation through May 26, 2024.

contract.note: The cited report reasonably identifies the compute pledge behind Marcus's broader wording. Assessing delivery under that pledge's actual terms is fair; team shortages and an unfinished four-year commitment alone do not establish breach.

evidence.note: The company disclosure establishes the compute baseline, purpose and four-year duration, but supplies neither delivery records nor an interim deadline.

Anonymous sources report shortages for the Superalignment team and uncertainty about allocation timing. This does not establish allocations across all qualifying work or a missed contractual deadline.

Contemporaneous reporting describes reassignment of the team's work and resource struggles. Dissolution therefore does not establish abandonment of the underlying commitment; no comparable allocation figures are supplied.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes the pledge and reported team shortages, but neither company-wide delivery nor failure under the pledge's terms by May 26, 2024. No interim allocation schedule or conclusive abandonment is established. The evidence therefore settles neither support nor contradiction.
